summary.headline: Torrent Pharma Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 51% to INR4,979 crores, with EBITDA margin at 33.5% and JB integration weighing on JB's international sales.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR4,979 crores (up 51%) and operating EBITDA was INR1,666 crores (up 54%), a 33.5% margin. Torrent's base business grew 18%, with India base business up 20% against IPM growth of 12%, while the underlying JB business was flat at INR1,086 crores after post-merger integration. JB India branded grew 7% (13% in Q1), while JB international fell 7% due to deferred deliveries from plant and quality integration. Management expects JB growth to return to double digits in H2 and cost synergies (INR450 crores) to be achieved about a year earlier than the original three-year plan.

segments.name: Torrent India base business
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,181 crores, up 20% vs IPM 12% (PharmaTrac), helped by launches and field force expansion. Curatio grew 34% in Q2 and H1 and is now 7-8% of base India business excluding JB.

segments.name: JB India branded
segments.commentary: Grew 7% in Q2 after 13% in Q1; management expects H2 above the H1 rate of about 10%, with India ahead of double-digit growth.

segments.name: JB international
segments.commentary: Down 7% from deferred deliveries linked to plant network optimisation and quality system alignment; recovery expected to take longer, with total JB growth guided to double digits in H2.

segments.name: Brazil
segments.commentary: Constant currency revenue BRL236 million, up 21% YoY; IQVIA market growth 5.7% vs Torrent 26%. Growth split roughly equally across price, volume and new launches. Management expects mid-teens growth ahead.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Constant currency revenue USD44 million, up 13%, driven by new launches meeting or exceeding share targets. Management expects pricing pressure in H2 as new competitors enter.

segments.name: Germany
segments.commentary: Constant currency revenue EUR26 million, down 13%, due to loss of high-value tenders, supplier disruption and government-mandated price cuts. Best case a slight decline in coming quarters, stabilising after 3-4 quarters.

segments.name: Rest of world (JB)
segments.commentary: Philippines, Mexico, Russia and South Africa growing high single digit to double digit; management suggests 6-9% for planning.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 EBITDA margin should be a little above 33.5%; management did not give a number but said margin can improve gradually.
JB total business growth expected to return to double digits in H2 FY27, with India branded above double digits.
Cost synergies kept at INR450 crores; expected to be achieved in about two years rather than three, with any upside to be confirmed after a couple more quarters.
Revenue synergies in India expected to show a reasonable improvement next year; international revenue synergies take two to three years due to filing timelines.
R&D intensity to stay within 4-4.5% of revenue next year, with the US filing push temporary over 2-3 years.
Brazil expected to grow mid-teens near term; Germany best case slight decline.
No EBITDA guidance for FY28; management plans to guide in Q1 FY28.
IPM growth expected at least 10% next financial year, possibly 1-2 points lower than the current year's around 12%.
capex_capacity: Combined India field force at 9,100 MRs at end of Q2; no change planned through FY27, with base business expansion of about 500 MRs possibly needed, taking the count to 9,500-9,600 next year (review in a couple of months).
Semaglutide injectable supply was disrupted for nearly two months; a new manufacturing partner was onboarded and supplies were fully restored by September.
Brazil has 53 molecules under ANVISA review; approvals take at least two years.
US filings: four products filed year-to-date, with four to five more expected before fiscal year end.
demand_pricing: India IPM grew about 12% YTD this year, which management views as possibly a one-off; it expects at least 10% next year.

Semaglutide: Torrent India holds 32% combined oral and injectable share in Q2 and above 90% of oral generics; minor injectable share loss expected to be recovered. Management sees generic semaglutide market around INR800 crores in year one and a path to INR2,000-2,500 crores over three to five years.
US pricing: no major change in market dynamics; new competitors expected on recent launches in H2, leading to price erosion. Base business is roughly flat, with growth from new launches.

Brazil competition is intensifying: local players with larger field forces and rising price competition over the past two to three years. Brazil semaglutide: one local generic launched about three months ago; Torrent expects to launch within 6-9 months.
Management says branded semaglutide prices should stay stable or rise gradually.

qa_highlights.question: How will JB recover in India and internationally, and will the international slowdown take longer?
qa_highlights.answer: Aman Mehta said India JB branded was 13% in Q1 and 7% in Q2 as guided. Growth is expected to rise each quarter, with H2 above the 10% H1 rate. International recovery may take longer, but total JB growth should be double digit in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Are cost synergies ahead of plan, and is there upside to the INR450 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhir Menon said about half of the INR450 crore could be realised this year and most by next year. Management is keeping the INR450 crore target for now and will review any upside in a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sequential JB margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Aman Mehta said field force merger savings were the largest driver, with procurement savings a smaller contributor. Margin improvement is expected to continue quarter-on-quarter for two to three more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the group EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhir Menon said H2 should be a little above 33.5%. He declined to guide FY28 and said guidance would come in Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will R&D spend stay elevated?
qa_highlights.answer: Aman Mehta said the step-up reflects more US filings for 2-3 years, and R&D should stay between 4% and 4.5% of revenue next year.

qa_highlights.question: How should the US outlook be read given price erosion and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Gupta said the base business is roughly flat, with growth from new launches. He expects pricing pressure in H2 as competitors enter, but volume and launches should keep growth positive.

risks_watch: Recovery of JB international deliveries and whether H2 double-digit JB growth is achieved.
Injectable semaglutide share recovery after nearly two months out of the market.
Germany: further decline from tender losses and government price cuts.
US price erosion in H2 as new competitors enter recent launches.
Brazil: entrenched local competitors and more aggressive price competition; ANVISA approval timelines of at least two years.
Novartis India changes affecting the JB ophthalmology deal; second tranche of about INR950-960 crores due December 2026 (management says the contract is clear).
summary.management_tone: Confident on India and synergies, with specific numbers and an upbeat view on Brazil and semaglutide. Cautious and more evasive on Germany, JB international timing, the cause of the IPM growth spike, and FY28 margin guidance, where management declined to give numbers.
key_quotes: So, it's largely driven from the India field force divisional merger that has been implemented, and also there has been further improvement in in procurement savings as well.
Instead of three years, I think we should be able to get there in two years' time.
We believe the impact is transient due to one-time nature of integration requirements, which were unavoidable.
I would think we'll maintain the current synergy view on INR450 crores.

adds.what: Combined India field force expansion of about 500 MRs (to 9,500-9,600) possibly needed next year; 9,100 MRs flat through FY27

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 EBITDA margin slightly above 33.5%, JB total growth back to double digits in H2 (India branded above double digits), IPM growth at least 10% next year; backing is largely share gains, Brazil/US launches and cost synergies (INR450 cr, now two years), with only a possible ~500 MR field force addition and no specific capacity numbers, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides H2 FY27 EBITDA margin a little above 33.5% (Q2 33.5%, Q1 33.8%), with JB margin still improving QoQ for 2-3 more quarters from field force merger savings.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Field force held at 9,100 MRs through FY27; about 500 more MRs (to 9,500-9,600) possibly needed next year, with review in a couple of months. No plant capacity numbers were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: JB total growth guided back to double digits in H2 (H1 about 10%, Q2 JB India branded 7%), India IPM growth at least 10% next year, and Brazil guided mid-teens.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No plant or capex plan discussed; only a possible ~500 MR field force addition next year, and no utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Cost synergies may beat the INR450 crore target (about half realised this year, most next year), with any upside to be reviewed after a couple more quarters.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: JB international fell 7% on deferred deliveries and JB growth must return to double digits in H2; US pricing erosion is expected in H2 and Germany is still declining 13%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: US filings of four products YTD with four to five more expected before FY end; Torrent expects a Brazil semaglutide launch within 6-9 months.

rows.label: Brazil ANVISA approvals (53 molecules under review)
rows.why: 53 molecules are under ANVISA review, but approvals take at least two years, so no near-term revenue from them.

rows.label: JB merger cost synergies INR450 crore in two years
rows.why: Target is held at INR450 crore and brought forward to about two years from three; about half is expected this year and most by next year.

rows.label: Semaglutide generic India market build-out
rows.why: Torrent holds 32% combined oral and injectable share and above 90% of oral generics; injectable supply was restored by September after a two-month disruption, and management sees a path to INR2,000-2,500 crore over 3-5 years.

tone.note: Management was confident on India growth (+20% vs IPM 12%), cost synergies and the Brazil/semaglutide story, but cautious and evasive on Germany, JB international timing, the IPM spike and FY28 margin, where it declined to give numbers. Analysts pushed on JB recovery, US pricing and R&D intensity.
